references.text: Verse 9 describes God's command that the water under the sky should gather to one place so that dry land appears, which is the direct occasion for the naming in verse 10.
Psalm 33:7 describes how God gathered the waters of the sea into a heap and laid the deeps in storehouses, reflecting God's organization of the water masses in Genesis 1:10.
Psalm 95:5 confirms that the sea belongs to God because he made it, and his hands formed the dry land – a direct reference to the creative acts in Genesis 1:10.

Psalm 104:5-9 elaborates on how God laid the earth's foundation, covered it with the deep as a garment, and set boundaries for the water so that it would not again cover the earth – a poetic expansion of Genesis 1:10.
In Exodus 20:11 it is stated that God created the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them in six days, which includes the actions described in Genesis 1:10.
Jeremiah 5:22 says that God set sand as an eternal boundary for the sea which it cannot cross, relating to God's arrangement of the water masses and the dry land in Genesis 1:10.

Job 38:8-11 poetically describes how God set doors and boundaries for the sea when it burst forth, saying 'thus far you shall come, but no further', which directly relates to the separation of land and sea in Genesis 1:10.

Proverbs 8:29 speaks of God setting a boundary for the sea so that the water would not transgress his command, and establishing the earth's foundations, relevant to the creation of land and sea in Genesis 1:10.
The psalm calls created elements (sea and dry land) to praise, based on their origin in creation.
